title: Photoporation-mediated spatial intracellular delivery of stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
author: Léger, De Clercq, et al.

steps.title: Prepare iPSC‑derived cardiomyocytes
steps.instruction: Differentiate human induced pluripotent stem cells to cardiomyocytes using the adapted Burridge et al. protocol (Supplementary File 1) and culture until day 30, when a pure cTnT‑positive, Nkx2.5‑positive population is obtained.

steps.title: Seed cells in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Plate the day‑30 iPSC‑CMs into a standard 96‑well tissue‑culture plate at the desired density (as used for the optimization experiments).

steps.title: Prepare gold nanoparticle suspensions
steps.instruction: Make four AuNP solutions in cell‑culture medium at final concentrations of 1 × 10⁷, 2 × 10⁷, 4 × 10⁷, and 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Add AuNPs to wells
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate AuNP suspension to each well so that the final AuNP concentration matches one of the four target values (1 × 10⁷, 2 × 10⁷, 4 × 10⁷, or 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Add FITC‑dextran cargo
steps.instruction: Introduce FITC‑labelled dextran of either 10 kDa (FD10) or 150 kDa (FD150) into the wells. FD150 is only tested with the two highest AuNP concentrations (4 × 10⁷ and 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Set laser parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the photoporation laser to one of three fluences: 0.77 J · cm⁻², 1.16 J · cm⁻², or 1.60 J · cm⁻². For spatially selective delivery, program the beam to scan a heart‑shaped pattern instead of the whole well.

steps.title: Perform photoporation
steps.instruction: Irradiate each well (or the defined region) with the selected laser fluence while AuNPs are present, thereby generating vapor nanobubbles that create transient pores in the iPSC‑CM membranes.

steps.title: Include experimental controls
steps.instruction: Set up the following controls in parallel: (i) non‑treated control (NTC) – no AuNPs, no laser, no cargo; (ii) FD10/FD150‑only control – add cargo without AuNPs or laser to assess passive uptake; (iii) AuNP + laser control – apply AuNPs and laser without cargo to evaluate photoporation toxicity.

steps.title: Post‑irradiation incubation
steps.instruction: Allow the cells to recover for the appropriate time (as used in the validation experiments) before downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quantify delivery by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Harvest cells and stain with TO‑PRO‑3 to exclude dead cells. Using a MACSQuant 16 flow cytometer, determine the percentage of FITC‑positive single cells within the viable (TO‑PRO‑3‑negative) population. Record the relative mean fluorescence intensity (rMFI) by dividing the MFI of FITC‑positive cells by the MFI of the NTC.

steps.title: Measure cell viability
steps.instruction: Perform a CellTiter‑Glo® assay on each well to obtain a viability read‑out (expressed as a percentage of the NTC).

steps.title: Calculate delivery yield
steps.instruction: For each condition, multiply delivery efficiency (percentage of FITC‑positive viable cells) by viability to obtain the overall yield.

steps.title: Record expected performance metrics
steps.instruction: Document the observed results: FD10 delivery efficiencies up to 59.7 % ± 1.8 % (at 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹); FD150 delivery performed only at 4 × 10⁷ and 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹ with a laser fluence of 1.16 J · cm⁻²; the highest overall yield (40.9 %) obtained with 8 × 10⁷ AuNPs · ml⁻¹ combined with 0.77 J · cm⁻²; note occasional cargo uptake outside the irradiated region, likely from permeabilized apoptotic cells.
